comments.note: handleListRepos uses a sequential for-loop to validate undeclared namespaces (api-repos.ts L243–259), calling LedgerStore.listProjectsByFolderNames() once per namespace. For ledger roots with many undeclared directories, a Promise.all() parallel fan-out would reduce latency. The current approach is safe and correct; the sequential pattern is consistent with other handler functions in this file.

The synthetic RepoListItem entries for undeclared repos set created_at and last_modified to new Date().toISOString() at query time (api-repos.ts L248). If the frontend sorts by these fields, the order of undeclared entries will vary between requests. A stable sort key (e.g., namespace name) or a sentinel value (epoch) might be preferable. This is a product/UX decision outside this WP's scope.

The WP spec uses 'include_undeclared' (snake_case query parameter) while the internal TypeScript parameter is named 'includeUndeclared' (camelCase). The mapping is clear and explicit at server.ts L1249, following the same convention as other query params in the file (e.g., repository_name → repositoryName). No issue, just worth noting for consistency documentation.

comments.note: No blocking issues — code is clean and consistent across all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context).

The declared: boolean field on RepoListItem is a clean, non-breaking additive extension. Existing consumers that destructure only known fields are unaffected; frontend code that needs to distinguish declared vs. undeclared entries now has a first-class field to branch on rather than relying on heuristics.

The readdir error catch-and-degrade pattern (api-repos.ts L224–229) is the correct resilience choice for a filesystem discovery operation: a missing or unreadable ledger root should not fail the declared-repo listing. Comment on the catch block is clear.

Sequential for-loop over undeclaredNamespaces (api-repos.ts L243–259) is correct and intentional. For a GUI API handler — not a hot path — the sequential approach is simpler and easier to reason about than Promise.all(). If this ever becomes a performance concern at scale, a Promise.all fan-out is a straightforward refactor. The Developer's own note on this is accurate.

Synthetic timestamp assignment (new Date().toISOString() at query time, api-repos.ts L248) is an acknowledged product/UX tradeoff noted by the Developer. If frontend sort stability for undeclared entries becomes a concern, a sentinel epoch value or lexicographic sort by namespace name is the fix — both are trivial. No action required in this WP.
